sentences.text:
?Court No. - 28
Case :- U/S 482/378/407 No. - 5978 of 2019
Applicant :- Ahmad Umar

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. & Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Mohd. Ahsanussamad Faridi,Afaq Zaki Khan
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Virendra Kumar-II,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for petitioner, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2.  It is submitted by learned counsel for petitioner that on 19.4.2016 at 2:45 p.m. Food Safety Officer/complainant searched shop of Bablu and collected sample of Gutkha (Megha Sri Brand) four packets.
The notice of form 5A was not provided to the petitioner and co-accused Bablu.
It is further submitted that co-accused and the petitioner are separate licensee to sell Gutkha (Megha Sri Brand).

It is further submitted that on the basis of statement of co-accused Bablu, the petitioner has falsely been implicated in this case showing owner of the shop situated at Nanpara Market.
3.

It is further submitted that the provisions of Section 42 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 were not complied with and sample was not analysed by food analyst within fourteen days.
The Food Analyst found that sample contains Gambier and Tobacco, Tabacco is injuruous to health.
Hence the sample is misbranded, substandard and unsafe for consumption.
The violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2. (8,9 & 10) of FSS (Packaging & Labelling) REgulation, 2011 was also found.
Therefore, sanction for prosecution was granted by the Designated Officer i.e. Commissioner of Food Safety.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the petitioner was not the owner of the shop inspected by the Food Safety Officer.

Therefore, the proceedings of Case No. 7397 of 2016 under Section 26, 51, 52 & 59 of Food Safety & Standard Act, 2006 pending in the court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-I, Bahraich be quashed and non-bailable warrants issued against the petitioner be set aside.

5. Learned A.G.A. has opposed this petition by submitting that it is apparent on perusal of complaint that co-accused Bablu was employee of the shop inspected and searched by the Food Safety Officer and Ahmad Umar was found owner of the shop.
The Food Safety Officer tried to give copy of notice of Form 5A to the co-accused, who refused to sign this notice.
On the other hand, Food Analyst Varanasi analysed the sample on 3.5.2016 and submitted report.
Therefore, provisions of Section 42 (2) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 were complied with.

6. As far as learned counsel for petitioner has submitted that separate licence was issued in the name of Ahmad Umar, owner of Kirana Store and separate licence has been issued by competent authority in the name of Faiz Ahmad son of Mohd. Umar, who is Bablu according to facts narrated in the complaint.
7.

Learned counsel for petitioner has pointed out that there is complete violation of Rule 2.4.1(4) of Food Safety & Standards Rules, 2011 because no notice was issued or given to the manufacturer,
distributor or suppliers and the same responsibility has been levelled only against the business operator.

8. The petitioner may apprise the trial court regarding violation of this rule and he may also take the defence that separate licence has been issued in name of the petitioner and he is not the owner of shop on which co-accused Bablu son of Mohd. Umar was found at the time of inspection.
9. The petitioner shall be at liberty to apply before the trial court on the basis of these facts.

The factual aspects as argued by learned counsel for petitioner cannot be evaluated or analyzed during proceedings under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
10.
This petition is dismissed.
11. Learned counsel for petitioner further submitted that sometime may be granted to the petitioners for surrender before the trial court.

12. Considering the above submissions made on behalf of the petitioner, it is provided that if the petitioner appears and surrenders before the trial court within fifteen days from today and applies for bail in the abovementioned case, the trial court shall decide the bail application of the petitioner expeditiously, according to the exposition of law propounded by this Court and Hon'ble Supreme Court.
13. In the meanwhile, learned trial Court shall not adopt any coercive methods against the petitioner.
